summary.text: 车 is the modern simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a wheeled vehicle. Its shape derives from cursive writing of 車.

formation.text: The traditional graph 車 depicts a vehicle through selected features such as wheels, body or frame, axle, yoke, pole, and crossbar. Early forms varied, while later writing reduced and regularized the picture. 車 is a whole-graph pictograph, not a compound of separately analyzed parts; 车 is its later simplified graphic form.

components.text: 车 is the modern simplified character, derived from the cursive form of 車, attested by the Sui dynasty at the latest and standardized in 1956. It is the simplified whole graph, not a component of the vehicle picture.

history.text: Early oracle-bone and bronze forms of 車 varied in which vehicle features they showed. Later writing selected and regularized features into the traditional graph. The curated oracle-bone, Western Zhou bronze, and seal-script images illustrate different presentations; they are modern redrawings, not artifact photographs.

The modern form 车 derives from cursive 車, attested by the Sui dynasty at the latest, and became a standard character in 1956. This modern simplification is distinct from the variation and reduction seen in earlier forms of 車.

uncertainties.text: Descriptions support variable early depictions of vehicles, but specific details in any one redraw should be treated cautiously.
Early inscription examples are identified by corpus references, but the cited evidence gives neither calendar dates for those individual inscriptions nor a precise earliest date for the graph.

senses.text: Reported oracle-bone examples use 車 for vehicles, and bronze examples include vehicles and war chariots. These establish early vehicle-related use, though not a calendar-dated first occurrence.
An oracle-bone example is identified as a place-name use. The evidence does not explain the name or connect it historically to the vehicle sense.

senses.gloss: wheeled machines; transporting by cart; cartload measure
senses.text: Later dictionaries record these uses, but the evidence does not date their emergence or establish a continuous development from the vehicle sense.
The common modern meaning includes vehicle and car.

limitations.text: The chronology and semantic links among later machinery, transport, and measure senses are unresolved, so no chain of development is proposed.

Several proposals connect the spoken word represented by 車 with Indo-Iranian wheel or chariot vocabulary. Such borrowing would mean that a sign for an older word was reused to write a similar-sounding word; it would not be a change in the picture’s meaning. The depicted vehicle’s spoken name is not independently established here, so the proposed sound match remains disputed.
The traditional account that Xi Zhong made the vehicle in the Xia period is not independently confirmed by the cited evidence.

overview.text: 车 is a simplified way to write 車, whose early forms pictured a wheeled vehicle. Its modern shape comes from cursive writing of the traditional character.

components.text: This is the simplified character’s whole form, derived from cursive 車; it is not a separate part of the vehicle picture.

relationships.text: 车 is the modern simplified character derived from cursive 車.
